slot.brief: rms speed scaling with molar mass at same temperature; compare two gases

stem: At the same temperature, the rms speed of methane molecules is $500$ m s$^{-1}$. Given molar masses of methane and helium as $16$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $4$ g mol$^{-1}$, respectively, the rms speed of helium molecules is:

verdicts.working: At the same temperature, rms speed varies as the inverse square root of molar mass: v(He) = 500√(16/4) = 1000 m s⁻¹.

working:
$v_{\text{rms}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$ at fixed $T$
$\dfrac{v_{\text{He}}}{v_{\text{CH}_4}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{4}} = 2$
$v_{\text{He}} = 2(500) = 1000$ m s$^{-1}$

Independent check: At the same temperature, rms speed varies as the inverse square root of molar mass: v(He) = 500√(16/4) = 1000 m s⁻¹.
solution:
At the same temperature, $v_{\text{rms}} \propto 1/\sqrt{M}$. Thus,
$$v_{\text{He}}=500\sqrt{\frac{16}{4}}=1000\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$
